checks.item: 1b. Supervisor issues tokens only for boundaries it actually retains
checks.evidence: src/xverse/maestro/native/bootstrap.c:345-346 kind 4 is the only path to respond(kind 20); watch_boundary src/xverse/maestro/native/bootstrap.c:188-198 checks slot order, frozen/empty/no-descendant cgroup, parent==boundary_parent, not already watched, not a helper child cg, then dups the fd and computes the token over the retained dup before appending it; any failure returns -1 and main exits via cleanup (src/xverse/maestro/native/bootstrap.c:351), so a stale watch_reply is never sent
checks.note: Helper cgroups cannot be watched (194) and role 4/5 cannot be born into a watched cgroup (221, 231), so no token exists for a helper cgroup.

checks.evidence: Token binds (st_dev, st_ino); src/xverse/maestro/native/run_authority.c:389 recomputes over fstat(fd) of the descriptor in the same request; src/xverse/maestro/native/run_authority.c:392-395 rejects any identity already present in any unit's history, so one watched boundary is admissible at most once
checks.note: The token is not bound to unit, slot or generation; see F02R-07.

checks.evidence: Supervisor keeps every watched fd open for its whole life (src/xverse/maestro/native/bootstrap.c:195-197; never closed outside process exit). An open fd pins the kernfs node, and kernfs releases the node id (idr) only on the final put, so the (st_dev, st_ino) of a watched-then-removed cgroup cannot be handed to a new cgroup while the supervisor lives; on 64-bit kernels kernfs ids are additionally allocated cyclically with a generation in the high 32 bits
checks.note: Reasoned from kernel behaviour, not tested. Residual only if the supervisor dies abruptly (no cleanup) while the authority survives; see F02R-04.

checks.evidence: src/xverse/maestro/native/run_authority.c:385-404 uses one received fd throughout: cgroup(fd,1), fstat(fd,&next), watched(g,&next,p+224), openat(fd,'..'), history comparison with next, F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC(fd), and stores next.st_dev/st_ino. The identity of an open fd is immutable, so the verified identity is exactly the admitted one; all checks precede the first mutation at 396-398
checks.note: cgroup state (frozen/populated) can still change after the check; that is pre-existing and not part of F-02.

findings.title: Watch key readable by the same-uid parent between execveat and PR_SET_DUMPABLE(0)
findings.scenario: The authority is born with CLONE_PARENT, so the Python peer is its parent. execveat resets dumpability to 1; the authority reads the key and keeps its fd open until line 288 and only becomes non-dumpable at line 316. The peer controls the timing (it sends ACTIVATE) and, with yama ptrace_scope=1 as on this host, may PTRACE_ATTACH to its own child or open /proc/<pid>/fd/<n> (n is visible in cmdline) in that window; an attachment survives the later prctl. A hostile peer could then mint tokens for any identity. A buggy-but-honest broker, the F-02 threat, does not do this, and a hostile peer can in any case obtain legitimate tokens by sending WATCH, so the gain is limited to boundaries that would fail watch_boundary's checks.
findings.recommendation: Call prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE,0) as the first statement of main, before initialize touches the key, and state in finding 403 that confidentiality against a hostile same-uid parent is not claimed (a loader window before main remains).

findings.title: No unit test of the relaxed kind-20 packet rule
findings.scenario: bootstrap.py:264 and 269 now admit a nonzero token with pid 0 for v2 kind 20 and require it; only kind 4 shapes are tested, so a regression that lets another kind carry a token with pid 0, or accepts a zero kind-20 token, would not be caught at the packet layer.
findings.recommendation: Add literal cases: v2 kind 20 with nonzero token accepted; kind 20 with zero token, with pid!=0, and v1 kind 20 rejected; kind 4 with nonzero token still rejected; another pid-0 kind (e.g. 19) with nonzero token rejected.

findings.title: Client-side ML-AFFA-WATCH-TOKEN check is not exercised
findings.scenario: test_affa_client.py:233 supplies a ticket but the boundary is unwatched, so the UNWATCHED check fires first; no test sends an ADVANCE for a watched boundary with a wrong ticket through _exchange, so the precondition and its no-send/no-sequence-advance behaviour are untested.
findings.recommendation: Add a client test with a watched boundary and a wrong nonzero ticket asserting ML-AFFA-WATCH-TOKEN, unchanged client.sequence and nothing sent.

findings.title: Token proves 'watched by this supervisor instance', not 'currently watched'; relies on the supervisor pinning the kernfs node
findings.scenario: The MAC covers only (st_dev, st_ino). Identity reuse is prevented because the supervisor never closes watched fds (bootstrap.c:195-197), which pins the kernfs node id, plus 64-bit cyclic kernfs ids. If the supervisor dies abruptly (SIGKILL, no cleanup) the authority, whose liveness check is the Python parent, keeps admitting tokens for up to its lease while no watcher exists. This is the general supervisor-liveness property rather than a token defect.
findings.recommendation: Record the kernel assumption and the supervisor-liveness dependency in finding 403; optionally give the authority a native liveness link to the supervisor (e.g. a pidfd) so ADVANCE is refused once it is gone.

findings.title: Late STAGE rejection is not independent evidence of non-admission; no supervisor-born negative control
findings.scenario: Any REJECTED closes the authority (run_authority.c:537), so the later STAGE is rejected whether or not a generation was recorded; non-admission actually follows from advance_unit returning before its first mutation (396-404) and from the empty new boundary. Negative cases use the harness key only; the supervisor-issued path is tested only positively (test_affa_epoch.py:53).
findings.recommendation: Word the evidence as 'REJECTED before admission, by code path, with an empty boundary' and optionally add one raw wrong-token ADVANCE through a supervisor-born authority.

findings.title: Finding 403 is accurate but incomplete
findings.scenario: (b) omits the all-zero key rejection and the seal/size checks; (d) omits the forged-token control; 'Python never receives the key' holds for the protocol but is qualified by F02R-01; the token's run-wide (not per-unit) scope (F02R-07) and the kernfs/supervisor-liveness assumption (F02R-04) are not stated.
findings.recommendation: Add these qualifications when 403 is next updated.

findings.title: Token is not bound to unit, slot or generation
findings.scenario: A token for a boundary watched for unit A is accepted on an ADVANCE for unit B, provided the authority's own checks pass (same parent as u->parent, identity unused in any history). The F-02 property (the supervisor watches the admitted boundary) still holds; intended unit binding remains a Python responsibility.
findings.recommendation: None needed for F-02; mention it if per-unit binding is ever claimed.

verdict_rationale: A Python caller that holds tokens but not the key cannot obtain a valid token for a boundary the supervisor did not WATCH, cannot replay one boundary's token for another, and the authority verifies the identity of the same open fd it admits. The remaining items are hardening (dumpable window), test coverage and documentation; none reopens F-02 for a non-hostile broker.
limits: Source reading only; kernel kernfs behaviour reasoned, not tested; no test was run and no binary executed.
